title: Reporting News and Writing Instructions
summary: Identify the parts of a news report and learn to understand and write clear instructions, step by step.
keyIdeas: Instructional texts explain how to do something in a clear order. In Spanish, they often use infinitives or commands.
News reports describe real, recent events and answer key questions: what, who, when and where.
A news report usually has a headline, an opening summary and a main body. It should present facts clearly and accurately.

activities.prompt: In PE, the teacher gives the class a sheet of dodgeball rules. What type of text is it?
activities.explanation: Game rules are instructional texts because they explain what to do to play the game.
activities.hint: Think about its purpose: does it tell you how to play or report a recent event?
options: An instructional text, because it explains the steps and rules for playing.
A news text, because it reports a recent event.
A poem, because it expresses feelings through rhyme.

activities.prompt: When writing a news report, the writer should invent fantastic details to make it more exciting.
activities.explanation: News reports should describe real events accurately, without making up information or imaginary characters.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish name for a part of a news report to its main purpose.
activities.explanation: The headline attracts attention, the opening summary presents the key facts and the main body gives more detail.

pairs.right: Presents the main idea in large, eye-catching letters.
The first paragraph, which summarises the most important facts.
Paragraphs that explain the details and what happened.

activities.prompt: Hugo and Aisha want to make fruit skewers. Put these Spanish instructions in a logical order.
activities.explanation: Instructions need a clear sequence: wash the fruit, cut it with an adult's help, put the pieces on skewers and serve them.
items: Lavar bien las manzanas, las fresas y las uvas con agua fresca.
Pedir a una persona adulta ayuda para pelar y cortar la fruta.
Insertar los trozos de fruta alternando colores en los palillos de madera.
Servir las brochetas en un plato limpio y disfrutar de la merienda.

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish text titles by text type.
activities.explanation: Recipes and manuals explain how to do something. News reports and journalistic interviews inform readers about events and topics.

items.text: Receta de tarta de manzana con canela
Inaugurada la nueva biblioteca municipal del barrio
Manual para montar una estantería de madera
Rescate con éxito de dos excursionistas en la sierra
Guía de pasos para plantar semillas de tomate
Entrevista a una científica sobre el cambio climático

activities.prompt: Complete this Spanish laboratory rule with the correct verb form.
activities.explanation: Spanish instructions often use infinitives, such as «llevar», «cortar» and «doblar», or commands to explain the actions required.
activities.sentence: Para evitar accidentes, es obligatorio ___ las tijeras con la punta hacia abajo.
options: llevar
llevaba
llevaste

activities.prompt: Find the problem. Lucía writes this Spanish instruction for an experiment: «Echa el agua azul en el vaso y espera». What is missing?
activities.explanation: A useful instruction is clear and precise. It should say how much water to use and how long to wait, for example five minutes.
activities.hint: Would you know exactly what to do just by reading the sentence?
options: The verb «espera» belongs in a news report and cannot be used in experiments.
Instructions can never contain the conjunction «y».
It is unclear because it does not say how much water to pour or how long to wait.

activities.prompt: Read this fictional school news report in Spanish and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Understanding a news report means identifying the main event, the people involved, and when and where it happened.
activities.title: Éxito total en el estreno del huerto escolar
activities.text: Ayer por la mañana, el alumnado de cuarto de primaria inauguró el huerto ecológico del colegio Cervantes. Durante dos semanas, niños y niñas limpiaron el terreno, colocaron bancales de madera y sembraron lechugas, zanahorias y fresas. La actividad contó con el apoyo de las familias y de la asociación ecologista del barrio, que aportó semillas tradicionales. La directora del centro felicitó a todos los participantes por su trabajo en equipo y anunció que la primera cosecha se recolectará en junio.

questions.prompt: What is the main event described?
questions.explanation: The report mainly describes Year 4 pupils opening their school garden.
options: A botany lesson in the town library.
A mountain trip organised by families.
The opening of the garden at Cervantes school.

questions.prompt: Who helped by providing traditional seeds?
questions.explanation: The text says that the local environmental association provided the seeds.
options: A distant garden centre.
The local environmental association.
The local police.

questions.prompt: Why is this a news report rather than an instructional text?
questions.explanation: It reports a recent event and answers basic questions about what happened.
options: It explains step by step how to build a wooden raised bed.
It contains an ordered list of gardening materials and tools.
It describes what happened, who took part and when, without giving instructions to follow.

activities.prompt: Omar writes this Spanish school news report: «El equipo de voleibol ganó la final por tres sets a dos tras un partido muy emocionante». What information is missing to answer «¿Cuándo?»?
activities.explanation: The question «¿cuándo?» asks when the event happened, for example «ayer por la tarde».
options: The colour of the players' shirts.
The name of the company that made the ball.
The day and time when the match took place.

activities.prompt: In this fictional exercise, volunteers removed 200 kilograms of plastic from Sol beach. Which Spanish headline presents that fact clearly?
activities.explanation: «Voluntarios locales retiran doscientos kilos de plástico de la playa del Sol» reports the fact. The headline starting «¡Qué asco!» expresses an opinion, and the other one offers instructions.
activities.hint: Look for a headline that says who acted and how much plastic they removed.
options: ¡Qué asco de playa, la gente tira demasiadas botellas de plástico!
Voluntarios locales retiran doscientos kilos de plástico de la playa del Sol
Pasos sencillos para no ensuciar la arena cuando vayas a nadar
